title: Path Traversal via Path.Combine Absolute Override
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET; behavior identical on Windows and Unix apart from drive-letter/root syntax
security_mechanism: Path.Combine is a string joiner with one documented trap: if the second argument is rooted (an absolute path like /etc/passwd or C:\Windows\x, or even a drive-relative \\path), Combine returns the second argument unchanged and the base directory is silently discarded. '..', '.', and reserved-device names pass through untouched, so a single Combine never confines the result to the base; File.Open/StreamReader then operate on an attacker-chosen path. Archive extraction (ZipArchiveEntry.FullName) reintroduces the same shape because entry names may carry '..' or rooted paths that Combine happily accepts.

source_sink_clues.source: Uploaded filenames, archive entry FullName values, download/path parameters, and any path component derived from a request.
source_sink_clues.sink: Path.Combine(baseDir, attackerPath) whose result feeds File/Directory/StreamReader APIs; ZipFile.ExtractToFile(entry, Path.Combine(dest, entry.FullName)) on untrusted archives

tracking_guards: Check for Path.GetFileName (or GetFullPath with a containment test) before Combine, and require the full-path containment check: Path.GetFullPath(candidate) must start with the base's GetFullPath plus the directory separator; for archives require entry-name validation that rejects rooted names and '..' segments before ExtractToFile.
not_candidate_when: The path component is generated server-side (GUID or sequence number), GetFileName strips directories and the GetFullPath containment check rejects escapes, or archive entries are validated/rejected for rooted and '..' names before extraction.
synthetic_safe_example: string clean = Path.GetFileName(userPath); string path = Path.Combine("/base/dir", clean);
public_references: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html
